overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not listing the Town Manager's Report topics with sufficient specificity, but found no violation on the closing-matters topic or the executive session minutes topic.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 28 notice topic 'Town Manager's Report' was not specific enough, though the Town Manager's memo listed many detailed matters the Board then discussed.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the Board was obligated to provide the public notice that it anticipated discussing these matters. Its failure to do so violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice topic 'Select Board Closing Matters - Topics to Include but not limited to' with 'Votes May be taken' was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not hold any discussions under this topic, we find no violation with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session notice citing all ten Purpose 21(a) clauls to approve May 27, 2025 minutes failed to identify the specific purpose.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that the additional detail “to consider and approve previous executive session minutes from May 27, 2025” provides sufficient notice to the public of the anticipated nature of the executive session discussion such that the public would know if the reason for convening in executive session was proper.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
